title: Vernetzte Schweiz 1860–1914
tagline: Address books · Telephone directories · Authority data
lead: Address books of Swiss towns and the early PTT telephone directories, linked to one another and to Wikidata, the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland (HLS) and the Integrated Authority File (GND).
sources_p: Each town is processed in its own repo and taken over here at a pinned version. Authority data are shown down to the «possible» tier; links that the check against the HLS article found to be wrong remain hidden.
phone_p: Entries per canton and year, by the resolved place of each entry. Up to 1910, directories newly processed entry by entry (batch A); 1911–1914, the nationwide volumes (batch B). «–»: place not resolved.

quality_p: In the 1911–1914 volumes the place is given as a heading, which was carried over to the following lines during reading. If a heading is missed, whole pages inherit the wrong place – Zurich 1912 appears as «Zwillikon (Affoltern a. A.)». Such runs are checked against the other years: the same subscribers usually appear in the book for several years.

kpi_linked: directory entries with an address book entry
links_p: A telephone directory entry is linked to the entries of the same person or firm in each address book volume of the town: same surname, then first name or initial, alliance name, street and house number, occupation and the telephone mark in the address book. A link is made only if exactly one person fits best; if first names or alliance names contradict each other, none is made. The larger the gap in years, the more evidence is required – sons and successors carry on name, house and business.
links_gap: Basel has only the 1862 volume, 19 to 52 years before the telephone directories: there the name alone almost never suffices, and the «certain» tier is not assigned.
links_recall: Recall, measured in Aarau on the entries that carry the telephone mark in the address book and whose surname occurs in the telephone directory within ± 2 years:

ent_p: Entries for the same person or firm are grouped into one entity across telephone directory editions and address book volumes, per municipality. Evidence is the same number, first name, address, occupation and the pairs from the address book linking. If first names or alliance names contradict each other, or if a widow and her husband, or a business and its successors, appear side by side, no grouping is made. The entities then receive authority data: taken over from the towns, otherwise via Wikidata and the municipality number.

ent_quality_note: Assessed by Claude against the printed text, not by the project staff. With 10–30 cases per layer, one case shifts the figure by 3–10 points.

pg_auth_note: «Probable» and «possible» are suggestions, not certainties. Whether the person in the directory is the person in Wikidata can only be shown by comparison with the sources.

pg_caveats: Telephone directories and address books were read and parsed by text recognition and language models. Names, numbers and addresses may be misread; the printed book is authoritative. Each entry gives its reference.

The telephone directory shows subscribers, not the population. Up to 1914 it was mainly firms, offices, doctors, inns and well-off households that had a telephone. Missing years mean missing editions, not missing connections.
The place of a directory entry is inferred from headings and exchanges (M1). Only entries with a certain or probable place are grouped and shown. The map dot marks the municipality, not the address.

Telephone directory and address book are linked in three tiers (certain, probable, possible). Measured on assessed samples, 80–100 % are correct depending on town and tier; the larger the gap in years, the less reliable.

Entries are grouped per municipality into the same person or firm. Father and son with the same name, widows and successors are separated where the entries show it; where not, they may be confused. If someone moves to another municipality, two entities result. Of the entries that reappear in the next edition, 75–92 % are measured to be linked there; the rest form an entity of their own.

Wikidata, HLS and GND links are «probable» (name, place and occupation match) or «possible». The towns matched their address book entries themselves and in part checked them against the HLS article. Rejected suggestions are not shown.

The samples from which the percentages derive were assessed by Claude (a language model) against the printed text, not by the project staff. The assessed cases, with reasons, are in the repo (data/review/).

Code and site are under the MIT licence. The contents of the telephone directories and address books up to 1914 are in the public domain: under the Copyright Act, directories arranged by alphabetical or geographical criteria generally lack originality (Art. 2 para. 1 URG), and where a work did exist, the term of protection has expired (Art. 29 para. 2 URG). Data and links are released under CC0 and may be freely reused. From the HLS we take only facts, no article text.
Baden, Bern, Lausanne, Zurich: not post-corrected

The address books of Baden (1900, 1910), Bern (1883–84, 1900), Lausanne (1896, 1907) and Zurich (1875, 1885, 1900, 1914) were read by the language model qwen3.8 without manual correction; in samples, 83–84 % of entries were fully correct in Bern, 93–96 % in Baden, and all 30 checked in Lausanne. The Baden 1910 scan lacks leaves (town of Baden from «Rü…», Bellikon, Bergdietikon up to «P»); the volume covers the whole district, and each entry counts for its municipality. In Bern, where many namesakes live in the same town, the rules are stricter: abbreviated streets («Kramg.») count as a street match, an initial plus the telephone mark is no longer enough for common surnames, and generic firm words («Schweizerische», «Café», «Bureau») need the same street. After this, 32 of 40 checked links were correct, 4 unclear and 4 wrong; «certain» 10 of 10. The 1907 Indicateur vaudois also covers the other Vaud communes; each entry's commune is taken from the heading in the book. In the Montreux district only entries naming a locality (Clarens, Territet …) are included. In Zurich the suburbs of 1875 and 1885 (Aussersihl, Riesbach …) count as the city; in the 1914 volume the last entries are missing on 11 pages. Of 30 Zurich links checked (1914), 27 were right, «certain» and «probable» 10 of 10 each.
pg_entries_merged: Identical lines from several editions of the same year are merged: {n} lines.
pg_occ_p: The search covers the occupation field of the entries, from the start of a word, ignoring accents: «Uhrmach» finds «Uhrmacher» and «Uhrmacherei». The directories are in German, French and Italian; «Metzger» does not find «boucher». A second word narrows it down («fabr horlog»). The slider selects years: results attested within that range.
pg_occ_hint: Enter at least three letters of an occupation.
pg_occ_map_note: Circle area = number of results in the municipality. Entities are counted, not entries; the dot is the municipality, not the address.
mp_telefon_p: Each person and each firm counts once, in the first year in which it appears in the directory. The slider selects a year or a range (drag both handles); clicking a bar selects a year. Filter by type, occupational class and canton.
mp_telefon_note: Read with care: the first year is the first surviving edition, not the year of connection. Up to 1910 only individual editions survive (batch A); 1911–1914, the whole of Switzerland annually (batch B). The jump in 1911 comes from this, not from a boom. The number of municipalities with entries in the selected range is shown below the map. This map counts the telephone directory only.
mp_berufe_p: Where were which occupations? «Count» shows the persons and firms of the class as a heatmap, «Share» the share of all entities in the municipality (only municipalities with at least 20), so that Zurich and Basel do not fill every map. Counted are those in the selected source within the selected range; the address books cover only Aarau (1884–1899) and Basel (1862).
mp_berufe_note: Occupational classes from keywords (medicine, hospitality, watches …). Measured on 60 random entities, 88–92 % are correctly classified; but around 40 % of entities have no class, and some of these list an occupation the keywords do not know. For a specific occupation: the occupation search.
mp_namen_p: Clicking a municipality shows the five most frequent surnames in the selected range and source. A name in the search field shows where persons of that name appear within the range, and the centre of gravity per year (red line, dots within the range larger).
mp_namen_note: The centre of gravity also moves because editions are missing or added: in 1911 the whole of Switzerland is added. A person counts for every year between their first and last entry, even if an edition in between is missing. Same name does not mean same family. Address books exist only for Aarau and Basel.

hl_h: From the HLS to the entry
hl_intro: Which persons in the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland (HLS) ought to appear in the telephone directories and address books of 1880–1914, and where do we find them? Expected are those who were adults in these years and lived or died in a place for which a book survives for these years.
hl_sum: {e} HLS persons expected; {s} found (authority data or probable), plus {c} with candidates to check.
hl_sum_note: Weighted by the measured hit rates, this is around 25 %. Many of those missing had no telephone or did not live at their place of death.
hl_s_text: place with year from the article
hl_s_long_text: The places come from statements with a year in the HLS article, plus the place of death.
hl_s_long_gelebt: The places come from Wikidata (residence or place of work), plus the place of death.
hl_s_long_nur_sterbeort: Only the place of death is known; it does not reliably say where the person lived in 1880–1914.
hl_cell_nobook: at this place, but no book for the year
hl_cell_out: outside the years at this place
hl_cands_p: Entities in the place with the same surname, listed in years in which the person was an adult. «Authority data» is a link from M3; all other tiers are suggestions.
hl_r_name_fehlt: The surname does not occur in our data, not even elsewhere. A misreading in the telephone directory is possible.
hl_r_name_nicht_am_ort: The surname occurs, but not in this person's places during their years.

hl_r_name_anderswo: Someone with the same surname and first name appears in another place (below). Perhaps the person lived there, perhaps it is a namesake.

meta_description: Address books of Swiss towns and early PTT telephone directories, linked to Wikidata, the HLS and the GND.
mw_p: Who disappears from one place and shortly afterwards appears for the first time in another? Same surname, compatible written-out forename, at most 6 years in between; the more that agrees (same occupation, title, rare name), the higher the tier. Only pairs that are unique in both directions count. Lines lead from the old to the new place (red dot); «Balance» shows arrivals and departures per place (green more arrivals, red more departures).
mw_note: Experimental: candidates, not verified moves. The phone books list subscribers only; «new in the book» often means «new telephone». Before 1911 only single editions exist, so cases cluster in 1911–1914. Pairs that are more likely a place-assignment error (same number, same address, street of the old place, neighbouring lines from the old place, alphabetically adjacent place) are excluded.
mw_seen: Both places covered before and after
mw_count: {n} possible moves, first year at the new place {y}, between {f} pairs of places.
